notes:
PRIMARY FINDING: this capability does NOT earn its '(PREFERRED bulk write)' label - as invoked through this surface, it cannot perform its one distinguishing feature at all. Every enveloped field it declares as type 'string' (tags, issues, priority, status, case_type, automation_state, automation_status, owner, preconditions, review_status, reviewers - i.e. every field except custom_fields) is rejected on every attempt with a 400 'Invalid JSON data' / "property ... of type string did not match ... object, null" - regardless of whether the payload sent for that field is the documented {operation,value} object (attempts 1-3) or a bare legacy array (attempt 4). Same failure on tags (add) and priority (ignore, no value) - reproduced 4/4 times across two unrelated fields and two payload shapes, so this is not a fluke of one field or one operation; it is the described type declaration itself (type:'string' for a field whose real shape is an object) causing the request to be rejected before the operation semantics can even run. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TASK: add/remove/replace/empty/ignore on tags could NOT be exercised - not add-preserves-existing, not remove, not replace/empty for silent-discard risk, not ignore-vs-omit. None of it is reachable. The safety claim over v1 (add/remove instead of destructive full-replace) is unverifiable in its current state, and in practice the capability is currently WORSE than v1 for tags: v1's bulk_edit_test_cases at least accepts a write; this one accepts none for tags.

SECOND FINDING (the one field that IS invokable returns the wrong response entirely): custom_fields is declared type 'object' rather than 'string' and is the only combination that reached the API (a no-op {'1':{'operation':'ignore'}} against a project with no field id 1 configured). It returned 200, but the body is not the declared {success, async, unique_id} bulk-edit ack at all - it is a project-wide test-case LISTING (test_cases[], folders{}, info{}, filter_details{}, workflow{}) covering all 30 cases across every folder in the project, including __readonly__ (764093) and TC-54455. This is a wholesale response-shape mismatch, not a missing/extra key. Read-back confirms no data was actually changed on any case other than TC-54489 (whose last_updated_at alone moved, to the call's own timestamp; its tags stayed ['mcp-probe'] and custom_fields stayed [] throughout) - so the mismatch is in what is returned, not in what got mutated. Still, returning a full unfiltered project listing (which happens to include the two protected/off-limits ids, TC-54455 and the __readonly__ folder) from what is supposed to be a scoped bulk-edit response is worth flagging to the product team as a real information/response-shape leak, independent of the type-string bug above.

THIRD FINDING (partial failure, third distinct behaviour): ids=[1985023 (real), 999999999 (nonexistent)] with the one working custom_fields no-op body produced a bare 404 {"success":false} - no `error` object, no code, no message, despite the capability's own declared 404 schema requiring one. This is a new (fourth) partial-failure behaviour among the bulk routes surveyed so far (silent 200 half-success x2, bare 404 x2 now with this one, 502 x1) and confirms 404-without-error-object is not a one-off.

What could NOT be tested as a result of the above: add vs remove tag semantics, replace/empty silent-discard risk on tags or issues, ignore-vs-omit distinction (ignore was only exercised on custom_fields/priority as a forced no-op, never contrasted against genuinely omitting the field, since any field present at all beyond custom_fields 400s regardless of operation), and any write-and-discard-cluster field (expected_result, estimate, metadata, test_case_dataset) - none of those are even parameters this capability exposes, so the write-and-discard question does not apply to v2's declared surface at all. What WAS confirmed clean: TC-54489 was not corrupted by any of the six attempts - tags, custom_fields, and steps are unchanged from baseline; only last_updated_at moved. No other case (including the protected __readonly__/TC-54455/TC-54458 set) shows a write-attributable timestamp change.
